name: standalone-class
intent: Make a class understandable, testable and reusable on its own by removing every dependency on other concepts of the surrounding model, so that its own definition is the complete explanation of its meaning.
problem: A class cannot be understood without loading the semantics of the classes it references: each dependency drags another concept into the reader's head, tests must assemble a slice of the model before they can run, and the class cannot be moved to another module or context because it carries its neighbourhood with it. The recurring decision is whether to keep the class coupled to the model for expressiveness, or to cut the dependency and lose the model's convenient vocabulary.
context: Applies inside a living domain model where reading one class means reading its collaborators: value-like concepts (Money, Percentage, Quantity, DateRange, coordinates, checksums) that many aggregates need, model classes that must be handed to another team or bounded context, and refactoring work that has to lift behaviour out of an entangled area. The decision fits where a class's meaning is intrinsic - determined by its own state and operations - and its collaborators can be replaced by primitives, standard-library types or types of the same kind.
benefits: Understanding is local: the class's definition is the whole explanation, and no other domain class has to be opened to predict what a call does.
Unit tests need no model: primitive inputs and the class's own type are enough, so tests are small, fast and read as examples of the concept.

Reuse across contexts: the class can move into another module, bounded context or shared kernel without dragging its old neighbourhood along, and a team that knows nothing about the surrounding model can still use it.

Fewer hidden coupling paths: implicit references add more cognitive load than explicit ones, so removing them also removes the failure mode where a change elsewhere silently changes this class's meaning.
It composes: operations that return the class's own type let clients combine instances without reaching back into the model (Closure of Operations).
The class becomes a natural unit of naming, review and documentation - a standalone class is exactly the piece of the model whose definition can be quoted in the ubiquitous language.
tradeoffs: Behaviour migrates to the caller: convenience methods that used to read a neighbour become the client's job, so the class gets simpler and the composition gets more complex - the coupling is moved, not deleted.

A rule that spans two concepts loses its single owner: if Money and Percentage must agree on rounding, a fully standalone pair has nowhere to state the rule once, so it is duplicated or a dependency is quietly reintroduced.

Framework and persistence friction: ORM mapping (JPA, EF Core, ActiveRecord), serializer and DI frameworks impose base classes, no-argument constructors, annotations or reflection-visible members; the standalone class usually needs a separate mapping layer or is weakened to fit.

Enforcement is by convention in most languages: nothing stops the next contributor from adding one import or one convenience method, and the class stops being standalone without a single test turning red.
Value semantics cost copies: staying context-free usually means immutable data and returned copies, trading allocation and copying for isolation.
Over-application produces anemic types: pushed to the extreme, 'no dependencies' degenerates into getters and setters plus services that hold all the logic, and the model loses its behaviour.
The assembly story becomes implicit: many individually trivial classes leave the question of who orchestrates them answered nowhere in particular.

participants.responsibility: The self-contained type: its operations and state description are the whole contract, and every type it names is a primitive, a standard-library type or its own type.
Uses the class through its own interface and must be able to construct, exercise and reason about it without instantiating any other model concept.
The only external vocabulary admitted into the class's interface (numbers, strings, dates, collections, ubiquitous value types); their context-free nature is what makes the class portable.

The language facility that makes the isolation enforceable rather than aspirational: private members, package or module visibility, file-private helpers, an opaque handle, a pimpl, a private module fragment or hard-private fields.
The rest of the domain model, which the class must not import; the relationships it would otherwise own are expressed by callers or by whatever composes the standalone classes.

use_cases: Value-like domain concepts shared by many aggregates: Money, Percentage, Quantity, DateRange, a coordinate or a checksum.
A class that must be handed to another team, a shared kernel or another bounded context without exporting the surrounding model with it.
Pure unit tests of domain rules: the class is built from primitives in a one-line fixture, with no repositories, factories or entity graphs.
Refactoring legacy code: lifting one coherent piece of behaviour out of an entangled transaction script into a class with no back-references.
Algorithmic domain types (interval arithmetic, unit conversion, rounding policy) used on both sides of a boundary.
Export or reporting projections that must stay stable while the write model keeps changing.
Teaching and review: a standalone class is a small, quotable unit of the ubiquitous language.

Shipped standard-library classes prove the pattern at scale: java.time.LocalDate is a final, immutable, thread-safe class whose whole API is primitives, its own type and interface markers - no framework, no base class, understandable and testable from its javadoc alone.

.NET's System.DateOnly (a struct with year/month/day in and DateOnly out of AddDays/AddMonths/AddYears) is a standalone value type that moved from an app-specific complaint into the BCL because it needs no surrounding model.
Rust's std::time::Duration is seconds plus nanoseconds with arithmetic returning Duration: usable by every crate without importing any domain vocabulary, exactly the portability the pattern promises.
avoid_when: The concept is defined by its relationships rather than by its own state - an aggregate root, a lifecycle entity, a tree or graph node: model it as Entity or Aggregate.
The rule genuinely needs several model objects at once (a Specification over an aggregate graph, a Domain Service): keep the dependency, name it and test it where it lives.

A framework requires the type to carry its mapping (JPA entity, EF Core entity, ActiveRecord model): accept the coupling explicitly or isolate it behind a Data Mapper instead of pretending the entity is standalone.
The class is only a data holder: call it a value object, a record or a DTO - the honest name changes the expectations.
Variation must be added from another module through subclassing or monkey patching: pick an explicit interface or strategy instead of relying on a boundary the language cannot enforce.
The team has no way to keep the boundary (no review, no test that would catch a new import): the class will silently decay into a normally coupled class.
anti_patterns: "God primitive": a class that absorbs foreign responsibilities (tax rules, formatting, persistence) to avoid dependencies, reimplementing concepts the model already owns.
Convenience creep: re-importing one other model type for a single helper method, which silently makes the standalone claim false.
Standalone as a synonym for anemic: getters and setters plus a service layer, presented as decoupling.
Public mutable fields or an open struct, so that "self-contained" ends up meaning "no encapsulation at all" and any client can put the object into an invalid state.
Copying a shared invariant into several standalone classes instead of extracting a value object or a shared-kernel type.
Framework annotations or base classes left on the model type, so the class can only be read with the framework documentation open beside it.
design_principles: Low coupling, high cohesion - when you can, go all the way and eliminate the other concepts from the picture (Evans).
Information hiding: the class's own definition is its whole contract, and implementation detail is invisible to clients.
Single responsibility: one concept per standalone class - a class with two concepts will need the other concept's vocabulary.
Depend on primitives and your own types rather than on a neighbour's public surface (interface segregation at the type level).
Composition over inheritance: no base class should be required for the type to acquire its meaning.
Value semantics by default: immutable data plus operations returning the type itself keeps results independent of context.
Ubiquitous language: the class name and its operations must be strong enough that no surrounding context is needed to interpret them.
best_practices: Keep public operations expressed in primitives, standard-library types and the class's own type; when a neighbour's type seems necessary, ask whether the needed knowledge can be passed as data instead.
Make the boundary real with the language's strongest mechanism (private members, module or package privacy, opaque handle, pimpl, hard-private fields) - a convention is not a boundary.
Validate in the constructor so that every instance is valid no matter where it came from, and keep invariants together with the type (Assertion).
Return the class's own type from its operations so clients can compose without reaching into the model (Closure of Operations).
Use the unit test as the detector: if a test needs more than the class and its primitives, the class is not standalone yet.
Record deliberate exceptions (a shared-kernel type, a framework type) as accepted dependencies so the next reader knows it was a decision and not an oversight.
Prefer a separate mapping or translation layer (Data Mapper, DTO) over weakening the class for persistence or serialization.
sources: Evans, Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software (2003) - Chapter 10, "Supple Design", STANDALONE CLASSES (pp. 188-190): eliminate all other concepts from the picture so that the class can be studied and understood alone, because interpretability degrades as dependencies are added.
